faq.q: What is the minimum age for a yacht charter in Marbella in 2028?
faq.a: There is no minimum age for children or teens on our Marbella yacht charters in 2028. Kids of any age are welcome on board. However, all children must wear a life jacket while on deck, and parents are responsible for supervising their children at all times. Our licensed skipper will brief you on safety rules before departure.

faq.q: Do you provide life jackets for children?

Children must stay seated while the boat is moving, and parents should keep an eye on toddlers near the rails. Our insurance covers all passengers, including kids.

faq.a: The jet ski included with the Mangusta 80 (Tier B, from €4,719/4h) can be used by teens aged 16+ with a valid license if they have one. Otherwise, a responsible adult must drive. The jet ski is a great addition for teens who want a bit more adventure alongside the main yacht charter.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food and drinks for kids?
faq.a: Absolutely. We already include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks on every charter. data.body_html:
Planning a family yacht charter in Marbella and wondering about the minimum age for kids and teens in 2028? Good news: there is no minimum age on our boats. Infants, toddlers, and teenagers are all welcome. Our Marbella yacht charter fleet, departing from Puerto Banús, includes boats from 6.4m to 29m, all with licensed skippers, safety equipment, and life jackets for every passenger. Whether you're cruising to Cabopino or anchoring at Cala del Faro, we've got you covered.

Our Minimum Age Policy for 2028

We do not set a minimum age for children or teens on any of our charters. That means you can bring a newborn, a toddler, or a teenager without restriction. The only rule: every child must wear a life jacket while on deck, and parents are responsible for supervision at all times. Our skippers will give a safety briefing before departure, covering where to sit, how to move around the boat, and what to do in an emergency. This policy applies to all boats in our fleet, from the compact Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the massive Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax).

Life Jackets and Safety Gear for Kids

We provide life jackets for all ages – from infants (5–10 kg) to teens (50+ kg). They are EU-approved, adjustable, and included free of charge. Let us know the ages and weights of your children when booking, and we'll have the right sizes ready. Every boat also carries a first-aid kit, fire extinguisher, flares, and a life raft. Our insurance covers all passengers, including minors. For toddlers, we recommend bringing a sun hat, UV-protective clothing, and plenty of sunscreen – the Andalusian sun is strong even in spring.

Best Boats for Families with Kids

For small families (up to 5 pax), the Dubhe (€749/2h) or Mariah SX21 (€749/2h) are affordable and easy. For larger groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are our Tier A family favourites at €749/2h to €2,299/8h. Both have a shaded flybridge, a small galley, and a bathroom. For teens who want more action, the Mangusta 80 (Tier B, from €4,719/4h) includes a free jet ski – perfect for older kids who want to explore the coast at speed. All boats depart from Puerto Banús, right next to Marbella's Golden Mile.

What's Included on Every Charter

  • Licensed skipper (speaks English and Spanish)
  • Fuel for the entire trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance covering all passengers
  • Safety equipment including life jackets for all ages
  • Spanish IVA (21%) – no hidden fees

All prices are per boat, not per person. So a family of 4 on the Astondoa 40 pays the same as a group of 9 friends. No extra charges for kids.

Popular Family Routes from Puerto Banús

Our skippers know the best spots for families. A typical 2-hour cruise goes west to Cala del Faro or east to Cala Cortés – both calm coves with shallow water for paddling. For a half-day (4 hours), head to Cabopino with its sandy beach and chiringuito, or Estepona for a longer swim stop. Full-day (8 hours) trips can reach Sotogrande or even Gibraltar (weather permitting). The sea is usually calmest from 10:00 to 14:00 – ideal for young kids. Bring a towel, swimwear, and a camera: dolphins are common along this coast.

Teens and Jet Skis on Tier B Charters

If you're chartering a Tier B boat like the Mangusta 80 (white or grey variant, 24m, 12 pax, from €4,719/4h), a jet ski is included free of charge. Teens aged 16+ with a valid license can drive it; otherwise, a responsible adult must be in control. The jet ski adds a thrill to the day – teens can race alongside the yacht, explore coves, or just have fun in the open water. It's a great way to keep older kids entertained while younger ones relax on board.

Booking and Pricing for Families

Ready to book? Check our full fleet and pick your boat. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, €1,299 for 4 hours, and €2,299 for 8 hours – all inclusive. For larger yachts like the Mangusta 80, pricing is on request via WhatsApp – we'll tailor a quote to your group size and duration. We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially during summer (June–September) when family charters sell out fast. No minimum age, no fuss – just a perfect day on the water with your kids.
